name: MINCHIATE
description: Minchiate (also known as Germini or Gallerini) is a historic Italian trick-taking game played with a unique 97-card Tarot deck. Invented in Florence in the 16th century, it was once one of the most popular games in Italy. The game features complex scoring for 'versicole' (card combinations) and a unique 'Fola' system where players can exchange cards before play.

content.text: Minchiate (also known as Germini or Gallerini) is a historic Italian trick-taking game played with a unique 97-card Tarot deck. Invented in Florence in the 16th century, it was once one of the most popular games in Italy. The game features complex scoring for 'versicole' (card combinations) and a unique 'Fola' system where players can exchange cards before play.

Minchiate was invented in Florence in the 16th century. The name comes from 'sminchiare' meaning 'to play a high trump', though some incorrectly associate it with vulgar meanings. The alternative name 'Germini' derives from Gemini (trump 35).
4 players in fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other.

97-card Minchiate deck: 40 trumps (numbered 1-40), four suits of 14 cards each (Cups, Coins, Swords, Batons), and the Fool (Matto). The top 5 trumps (Arie) are unnumbered: Trumpets (40), World (39), Sun (38), Moon (37), Star (36).
21 cards to each player in batches. The remaining 13 cards form the 'Fola' (talon).

items.text: Three-Player Minchiate: Each player for themselves with modified dealing.
Two-Player Minchiate: Modified rules for head-to-head play.
